stem.text: Use the limit comparison test with \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^{2}} \) to show that the series \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} a_n \), where \( a_n = \frac{\left(-1\right)^{n} \left(2 n^{2} + 6\right)}{6 n^{4} + 7} \), converges absolutely. State the conclusion, naming the series it concerns.

answer_key.label: \( \sum a_n \) converges absolutely, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{|a_n|}{1/n^{2}} = \frac{1}{3} \) is positive and finite and \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{2}} \) converges.

worked_solution.text: Compare the series of absolute values \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{2 n^{2} + 6}{6 n^{4} + 7} \) with \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^{2}} \), the p-series with \( p = 2 \), since the degrees of the denominator and numerator of the terms differ by 2. Both have positive terms.
The limit \( \frac{1}{3} \) is positive and finite, and \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^{2}} \) converges because \( p = 2 > 1 \).
\( \sum a_n \) converges absolutely, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{|a_n|}{1/n^{2}} = \frac{1}{3} \) is positive and finite and \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{2}} \) converges.

options.label: \( \sum a_n \) converges absolutely, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{|a_n|}{1/n^{2}} = \frac{1}{3} \) is less than 1.
options.derivation: the limit of the quotient compared with 1, as in the ratio test, and found less than 1

options.label: \( \sum a_n \) converges conditionally, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{|a_n|}{1/n^{2}} = \frac{1}{3} \) is positive and finite and \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{2}} \) converges.
options.derivation: the absolute and conditional labels exchanged after the series of absolute values was shown to converge

options.label: \( \sum a_n \) converges absolutely, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{|a_n|}{1/n^{2}} = \frac{1}{3} \) is positive and finite and \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{2}} \) converges.
\( \sum a_n \) converges absolutely by the alternating series test, because \( |a_n| \) decreases to 0.
options.derivation: absolute values never taken, so only the alternating series test was used and its result called absolute convergence
